//: A quadratic loop is made linear, measured, with the same output in the same order.
title: unique() runs fast on the benchmark and keeps every result and its order

files.bench.py:
import time

from dedupe import unique

items = list(range(10000)) * 2
start = time.perf_counter()
unique(items)
print(f'unique() of {len(items)} items: {time.perf_counter() - start:.3f}s')

import random

from dedupe import unique

random.seed(7)
for size in (0, 1, 5, 50, 500):
    items = [random.randint(0, size // 2 + 1) for _ in range(size)] + ['a', 'b', 'a']
    assert unique(items) == list(dict.fromkeys(items)), items

import time

from dedupe import unique

items = list(range(10000)) * 2
start = time.perf_counter()
unique(items)
elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
assert elapsed < 0.2, f'unique() took {elapsed:.2f}s'
